name: East Nyala
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Odden, David 2009 (Luyia-area phonology reference listed in Glottolog for East Nyala, p. 305); not accessible online

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages east2409 (East Nyala) and west2861 (West Nyala); reference record 307570 (Ochwaya-Oluoch 2003)
sources.note: East Nyala lists only Möhlig 1985 and Odden 2009 (subclassification) plus the two theses; West Nyala (Busia, Lake Victoria shore) cites Ochwaya-Oluoch 2003 pp. 7-8 for the two Nyalas being 'not mutually intelligible'. Glottolog links Ochwaya-Oluoch 2003 to East Nyala (hh:s:Ochwaya:Lunyala, grammar_sketch).

sources.citation: Osotsi, Eric M. 2020. A Systematic Reconstruction of the Phonology of Proto-Luyia: A Comparative Analysis. MA thesis, University of Nairobi. 127 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/11295/154048
sources.note: Sections 2.2.3 (pp. 21-22) and 2.3.3 (p. 28) give only the segmental phonemic inventory of 'Lunyala East' (24 consonants, 7 vowels); the whole thesis has no mention of stress, accent, prosody or suprasegmentals, and tone is mentioned only for Lubukusu dialects (p. ~12). Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Otunga, Catherine Sikuku. 2014. The Lunyala 'K' simple sentence: a Role and Reference Grammar analysis. MA thesis, University of Nairobi. 104 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/11295/75219
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Syntax (RRG) study of the Kakalewa/Lunyala 'K' variety of Navakholo constituency, Kakamega County (pp. 1-2). No statement on stress or accent; pp. 3-4 note a 'vacuum' of phonetic/phonological studies of Lunyala (K); p. 81 recommends future study of 'tone and how it marks tense and aspect'. (Only the repository's text-extraction bitstream could be downloaded; the PDF bitstream returned HTTP 500.)

sources.citation: Ochwaya-Oluoch, Yvonne E. 2003. A study of the phonology and morphology of Lunyala. PhD thesis, University of Sheffield, ix+320 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: The only full phonological description of (East) Lunyala: chapters on phonemic inventory, syllable structure, nominal and verbal tone; the most likely place for a statement on stress/accent vs tone. Glottolog attaches it to East Nyala; its pp. 7-8 discuss the two Lunyalas, so the variety described must be confirmed from ch. 1.
